prompt: A photorealistic photograph taken square-on to a laboratory bench of plain pale grey worktop against a plain white wall. On the bench lies a shallow grey tray holding flat RED plastic discs, all the same size, lying flat in a single layer, scattered irregularly inside the tray with a clear gap between every pair -- no two discs touching or overlapping, never in a row, never in a grid. On the plain WHITE MAGNETIC BOARD hanging above the bench, well away from the tray, flat GREEN magnets are stuck on, scattered irregularly and well apart -- never in rows, never in a grid, never gathered into little groups. The number of green magnets on the board must come out EXACTLY FOUR TIMES the number of red discs in the tray. You may choose how many red discs lie in the tray, as long as there are at least 12 of them. Nothing else anywhere in the picture is green or red, and there are no plants or leaves. Every counted object is FLAT matte single colour, evenly lit, with no glossy highlight and no printed pattern, and no two of them touch or overlap. Even light, sharp focus, seen flat-on with no perspective distortion, so every disc looks the same size as every other and every magnet looks the same size as every other. No text, no numerals, no labels.
